svg.title: Writing ડ
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ડ (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ડ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source note on variation: The teaching app animates ડ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper right, sweeps left across the high shoulder, descends through the middle into the right side of the broad lower bowl, then circles around its base and finishes at the lower-left terminal without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the high shoulder, descending middle transition, and broad lower bowl, but its printed shoulder is tighter and its bowl more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's shoulder-to-middle-to-lower-bowl order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the shoulder, transition, bowl, and terminal differently.
